children: Institutional risk appetite stayed constructive through August, according to State Street’s latest investor-flow indicators, marking a fifth straight month in positive territory and underscoring what the firm called remarkably resilient demand for risk assets.

The State Street Risk Appetite Index rose to 0.36 from 0.18 in July, its third-strongest reading of 2026. Equity allocations slipped only modestly and remained just off 25-year highs. The more striking portfolio shift was a rotation out of fixed income and into cash, as inflation worries, fiscal concerns, and rising term premia weighed on bond sentiment. By month-end, equity holdings stood 32.5% above bonds, versus a long-term average of 20% — a gap last seen in the run-up to the 2008 financial crisis. Cash allocations climbed to 17.6%.

Aggregate figures still conceal sharp differences underneath. Near month-end, flows gravitated back toward information technology even as virtually every other sector was sold. An extreme IT overweight persists alongside underweights elsewhere.

Overall, flow and positioning data continue to point to a pro-risk stance. Investors have favored cyclicals, emerging markets, carry strategies, and selected AI-linked markets while trimming certain defensives and traditional duration exposure. The picture is one of selective, rather than indiscriminate, risk-taking.

title: Risk appetite holds for a fifth month as institutions stay risk-on
